chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintaining kinship ties lightens the Reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and it is a delayer of the lifespan, and it protects from evil misfortunes; and charity given at night extinguishes the Anger of the Lord.'
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of maintaining kinship ties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores silat al-rahim not merely as a social duty but as a metaphysical safeguard that mitigates the severity of the final accounting and extends one's lifespan. The specific mention of 'night charity' (sadaqat al-layl) reflects the scholarly emphasis on the heightened receptivity of supplications and divine mercy during the quiet hours of the night, serving as a potent means to avert divine wrath.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Samad Bin Bashir who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The goodly relationships would ease the Reckoning on the Day of Judgement, and it is a delayer is the (termination of the) life-span and saves from the evil misfortunes; and the giving of the charity at night extinguishes the Anger of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 32. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ‘Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Maintaining good relations with relatives eases off the giving of accounts on the Day of Judgment, delays the coming of death and safeguards against misfortunes. Giving charity at night extinguishes the wrath of the Lord.’”
